recent_posts.title: The Future of AnduinOS, Entity, and Our Roadmap
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS founder announces plans to establish a commercial entity (AIURSOFT LIMITED) in Hong Kong to support enterprise clients while keeping the core OS free and open source. The roadmap prioritizes building package control infrastructure (PPA) to patch upstream Ubuntu bugs independently. The project will expand from a one-person operation to a proper team with on-call rotations and technical support, maintaining strict zero-data-collection and open source commitments while generating revenue through enterprise editions.

recent_posts.title: AnduinOS 1.3.9 can be upgraded to AnduinOS 1.4.2 today.
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS 1.3.9 users can now upgrade to version 1.4.2 using the automated `do_anduinos_upgrade` command. The upgrade is strongly recommended before January 30, 2026, when the upstream Ubuntu 25.04 base reaches end of life. The process takes 1-2 hours, migrates repositories from plucky to questing, downloads the new ISO, and replaces system files. Users must backup data beforehand as the upgrade may overwrite custom kernel configurations and initramfs modifications. Recovery commands are available if the upgrade fails.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS new build 1.3.9, 1.1.12 and 1.4.2
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS releases three new builds (1.4.2, 1.3.9, and 1.1.12) with shared improvements including updated apt sources for Brazil, enhanced video codec support via GStreamer plugins, improved repair script behavior, better error handling, and updated Intel audio device support. The 1.3 to 1.4 upgrade script will be available January 5th, 2026. In-place upgrades within the same fork version are supported via the do_anduinos_upgrade command, though cross-fork upgrades are not yet available.

recent_posts.title: Voxihost (AnduinOS hosting provider) was down.
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS services experienced a week-long outage starting December 31, 2025, affecting the website, documentation, system updates, and ISO downloads. The disruption was caused by a catastrophic NVMe firmware bug at hosting provider Voxihost, resulting in severe disk corruption. The OS itself remained functional as it doesn't require server connectivity to operate. The team is migrating to Vultr servers to restore services, with no data loss reported and ISO files recovered from backups.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS new build 1.3.8, 1.1.11 and 1.4.1
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS releases three new builds (1.3.8, 1.1.11, and 1.4.1) with printer and scanner support, improved hardware compatibility, system repair tools, and Russian localization updates. The builds add system-config-printer and scanning packages, refactor daemon code for better .desktop file handling, and introduce a do-anduinos-autorepair command for automated system fixes. Users can upgrade within the same fork version using the do_anduinos_upgrade command, while cross-fork upgrades (1.3 to 1.4) will be available January 1st, 2026.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS 1.4
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS 1.4 has been released, upgrading the base system from Ubuntu 25.04 to 25.10, with Gnome 49 and kernel 6.17. Key changes include dropping X11 support in favor of Wayland-only, switching to Firefox ESR, replacing the default terminal with ptyxis, and adding Romanian language support. The OS branding now identifies as 'anduinos' instead of 'ubuntu', requiring patches to maintain PPA compatibility. Direct upgrades from 1.3 to 1.4 are not yet supported, but a migration script is planned before January 2026 while version 1.3 remains under maintenance.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS new build 1.3.7 and 1.1.10
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS releases builds 1.3.7 and 1.1.10 with printer driver improvements and Linux kernel fixes. The distribution is collaborating with ArcMenu team and contributing to Blur My Shell plugin. Updates include adding printer-driver-all package for better printer support and removing Linux kernel version lock after upstream fixes. In-place upgrades are available via do_anduinos_upgrade command for dot releases within the same fork version.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS new build 1.3.6 and 1.1.9
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS releases new builds 1.3.6 and 1.1.9 with several improvements including removal of gnome-maps to reduce ISO size, upgraded ArcMenu extension with enhanced keyboard support, improved upgrade stability through new endpoints, fixed deskmon service crashes, added comprehensive printer driver support, and removed unnecessary blur-my-shell hacks that were upstreamed. The distribution continues using Ubuntu repositories while planning future integration with apt upgrade commands.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS new build 1.3.5 and 1.1.8
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS releases new builds 1.3.5 and 1.1.8 with bug fixes including GNOME control center logo display issues, Super+I settings shortcut problems, and taskbar display race conditions. Both versions add audio notification support and include kernel version pinning in 1.3.5. Users can upgrade using the do_anduinos_upgrade command, though cross-fork version upgrades are not supported.

recent_posts.title: Announcing AnduinOS new build 1.3.4 and 1.1.7
recent_posts.summary: AnduinOS releases new builds 1.3.4 and 1.1.7 featuring Japanese keyboard layout support, improved multi-display functionality, screenshot clipboard fixes, updated Intel audio firmware, and performance optimizations for the clipboard indicator plugin. The update includes switching to Huawei Cloud mirrors for Chinese users and various keyboard shortcut fixes.
